intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged wildlife including white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and Jesus Christ lizards. The hike concludes at a stunning Pacific beach for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest around the iconic Arenal Volcano, observing toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys up close. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by lush jungle, a perfect reward after a day of eco-exploration.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' This guided day trek through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unmatched chances to spot all four Costa Rican monkey species, Baird's tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and the endangered scarlet macaw in their pristine natural habitat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for your adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport arrival hall — look for a soda (local Costa Rican diner) or convenience snack stand. Budget ~$8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport shuttle in advance to save money vs. taxis. Shared shuttles cost around $15–25 USD per person. Keep small USD bills handy for tips. Don't exchange currency at the airport — rates are poor. Use a local ATM upon arrival for colones.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, explore the resort grounds and beachfront area. Take a morning walk along the beach to get oriented with your surroundings and enjoy the Pacific or Caribbean coastal scenery. Collect shells, watch for shorebirds like herons and pelicans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town or village on foot or by local bus (around $1–2 USD each way). Explore the central market, pick up a local SIM card for data, and browse small souvenir shops. Get familiar with the local layout and find budget eateries (sodas) for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset walk on the beach. Look for bioluminescence in the water if conditions allow. Head to a nearby local soda for a traditional Costa Rican dinner — try Casado (rice, beans, salad, and protein). Budget-friendly and filling.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort if included, or visit a local bakery (panadería) for pan dulce and coffee — budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Soda lunch in town — order a Casado or Arroz con Pollo. Budget ~$5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda near the beach — try Gallo Pinto with eggs or grilled fish. Budget ~$7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to help you recover from travel and get your bearings. Pick up a paper map or download offline maps for the region. February is dry season — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures around 28–32°C (82–90°F).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or mangrove path. Bring binoculars if possible — February is excellent for birdwatching. Look for toucans, scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and iguanas. Hire a local guide for ~$15–20 USD for a 2-hour guided walk for a much richer experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (entry fees typically $18–20 USD for foreigners). Explore the trails independently to save on guide fees. Look for sloths in cecropia trees, poison dart frogs, and coatis. Carry plenty of water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local farmers' market or fruit stand to stock up on cheap, fresh tropical fruits — mangoes, pineapples, papayas, and bananas for snacking throughout the trip. Enjoy a quiet evening watching the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Gallo Pinto (rice and beans with eggs) at a local soda — a classic Costa Rican breakfast. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the market — fresh fruit, bread, and local cheese. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using market finds if your accommodation has a kitchen, or dine at a budget soda. Budget ~$6–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book national park entry in advance online where possible — some parks have daily visitor caps. Wear neutral-colored, lightweight clothing for wildlife spotting. Apply insect repellent before entering any forested area.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING ADVENTURE DAY! Book a budget zip-line tour through a local operator (prices range from $45–75 USD depending on the number of lines and location — look for group deals or hostel-board specials). Most tours include safety gear and a guide. Enjoy soaring over the rainforest canopy with incredible views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, many operators offer add-on activities like a Tarzan swing, rappelling, or hanging bridges walk — ask about combo deals. Explore the surrounding cloud forest or jungle area on foot after the tour. Look for wildlife along the trails.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your zip-line adventure with a cold Imperial or Pilsen beer (Costa Rica's local beers, ~$1.50–2.50 USD) at a beachside bar. Share stories with fellow travelers. Enjoy a budget seafood dinner — fresh catch of the day is often affordable near coastal areas.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the tour — grab a filling breakfast at a soda. Budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Many zip-line operators offer lunch packages — ask if included or bring your own snacks. Budget ~$5–8 USD if buying
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant with fresh fish tacos or ceviche. Budget ~$8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining 1–2 days in advance to secure your spot. Wear closed-toe shoes (required), comfortable clothes, and tie back long hair. Leave valuables at the hotel — most operators provide lockers. Weight limits typically apply (usually under 250 lbs/113 kg).

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or shared shuttle to a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole (transportation ~$2–5 USD). Many waterfalls in Costa Rica have free or very low-cost entry. Swim in the natural pools, enjoy the mist, and take photos of the lush jungle surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the trail surrounding the waterfall area. Keep eyes open for wildlife — motmots, trogons, and leaf-cutter ants are commonly spotted. If near a river, look for Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks) running on the water surface.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort area. Explore the local nightlife scene — look for a local bar with live music (marimba or salsa). Many beach towns have free or cheap live music on Friday evenings. Enjoy a drink and mingle with locals and fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate at a local café. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic by the waterfall — bring snacks, fruit, and sandwiches prepared from market finds. Budget ~$4–5 USD
meals.dinner: Friday night street food — look for local vendors selling chifrijo (rice, beans, pork rinds, and pico de gallo) or empanadas. Budget ~$5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Always check waterfall trail conditions before going — some become slippery and dangerous after rain even in dry season. Wear water shoes if you have them. Never swim alone in natural water bodies. Bring a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Wildlife-focused morning: join a free or low-cost community-led wildlife tour or simply explore the beach at dawn. February is nesting season for sea turtles in some regions — check if your area has a turtle conservation project offering night or early morning tours (~$20–30 USD). Alternatively, look for howler monkeys in the trees near the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or reptile sanctuary if available in your region (~$10–15 USD entry). These smaller attractions offer up-close wildlife encounters with snakes, frogs, butterflies, and more. Very educational and budget-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday market evening — many Costa Rican beach towns have weekly markets (ferias) with local food, crafts, and produce. Stock up on cheap eats and souvenirs. Try local street snacks like patacones (fried plantains) and churros.

meals.breakfast: Pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh orange juice at a local soda. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Market lunch — grab a plate from a local vendor. Budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.dinner: Saturday feria street food feast — try multiple small dishes from different vendors. Budget ~$7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Check with your resort or local tourism office about any weekend events, free concerts, or community activities. Saturdays often have more local activity and are great for cultural immersion. Keep small bills for market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: REST AND RECHARGE DAY. Spend a lazy Sunday morning on the beach — swim, sunbathe, or read a book. Practice your Spanish with locals. Collect sea glass or shells. This is a great day to do laundry (look for a local laundromat — ~$5–8 USD for a full load washed and dried).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different stretch of coastline by walking or taking a local bus. Many Costa Rican beaches have tide pools accessible at low tide — check a tide chart and explore the marine life (sea stars, crabs, sea urchins, small fish).
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a budget meal at the resort if kitchen facilities are available, or enjoy a simple dinner at a local soda. Write in a travel journal, review photos, and plan the week ahead. Get an early night to prepare for more adventures.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer breakfast — try a local café with fresh fruit, yogurt, and granola. Budget ~$6–8 USD
meals.lunch: Simple and cheap — rice and beans plate or a sandwich from a local pulpería (corner store). Budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Quiet soda dinner — Casado with chicken or fish. Budget ~$7–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to charge all devices, back up photos, check emails, and research upcoming activities. Confirm any pre-booked tours for the coming days. Sunday is a good day to find locals relaxing at the beach — great opportunity for cultural exchange.

day_by_day.morning: ECO-ADVENTURE DAY: Book a mangrove kayaking or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) tour (~$25–40 USD for 2–3 hours). Paddle through mangrove channels and spot crocodiles, herons, egrets, and mangrove crabs. Many operators offer self-guided rentals for even lower cost (~$10–15 USD/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, visit a nearby organic farm or permaculture project. Many Costa Rican eco-farms offer free or low-cost tours where you can learn about sustainable agriculture, taste tropical fruits, and see how cacao, coffee, and pineapple are grown.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or food experience — look for community-based tourism operators offering traditional Costa Rican cooking classes (~$20–30 USD). Learn to make Gallo Pinto, plantain dishes, and fresh ceviche. Eat your creations for dinner!

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before kayaking — eggs, toast, and coffee at a soda. Budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh tropical fruit and snacks from the organic farm visit. Budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (included in class fee) or soda meal. Budget ~$20–30 USD (cooking class) or ~$7–9 USD (soda)

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen before kayaking and bring a hat and sunglasses — sun on the water is intense. A dry bag is essential for electronics. Book the cooking class or farm tour in advance — community-based tourism experiences often have limited spots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park not yet visited. Costa Rica has over 25% of its land protected — options may include Manuel Antonio, Tortuguero, Corcovado, or Arenal depending on your base location. Take a local bus or shared shuttle (~$5–15 USD). Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Hire a local certified guide at the park entrance for a 2–3 hour tour (~$20–30 USD) — they dramatically increase your chances of spotting wildlife like sloths, monkeys, and exotic birds. Many guides work for tips plus a base fee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon. Enjoy a refreshing swim at the beach or resort pool. Head out for dinner at a local restaurant — try Olla de Carne (beef and vegetable stew) or fresh seafood soup.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab a to-go breakfast sandwich (bocadillo) and coffee from a local café. Budget ~$3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for the park (no outside food in some parks — check rules) or eat at the park's budget cafeteria if available. Budget ~$5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner after a great wildlife day — local restaurant with a two-course meal. Budget ~$10–14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Some national parks require advance online reservations — check the SINAC (Costa Rica's national park system) website. Bring plenty of water, snacks, and insect repellent. Wildlife is most active in the early morning — aim to be at the park entrance when it opens.

day_by_day.morning: Canopy/hanging bridges walk — different from zip-lining, hanging bridges offer a slow, peaceful walk through the rainforest canopy at treetop level. Many operators offer self-guided hanging bridge walks for ~$20–30 USD. Excellent for birdwatching and photography without the adrenaline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local waterfall or hot spring in the area (natural hot springs near volcanic regions are often free or very cheap). Soak your muscles and enjoy the natural thermal waters surrounded by jungle. Bring a towel and change of clothes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local arts and crafts scene — visit a local artisan workshop or gallery. Many Costa Rican artisans create beautiful work from sustainable materials (bamboo, recycled wood, natural dyes). Window shop or pick up a small, meaningful souvenir.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and granola at a health-conscious local café. Budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside soda near the hanging bridges — rice and beans with grilled chicken. Budget ~$5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget Italian-Costa Rican fusion restaurant (common in tourist areas). Budget ~$8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wednesday mid-week is often less crowded at popular attractions. Take advantage of quieter trails for better wildlife encounters. If visiting hot springs, check water temperature — some natural springs can be very hot. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: ADVENTURE MORNING: White-water rafting or river tubing experience (~$30–60 USD for rafting, ~$15–25 USD for tubing). Costa Rica's rivers offer options for all skill levels. This is one of the country's top eco-adventure activities. Many operators include transportation and lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-rafting relaxation — visit a local beach or riverside swimming hole to cool off. Alternatively, explore a nearby town's central plaza, church, and local shops. Pick up local snacks like chifles (plantain chips) and palmito (heart of palm) products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner preparation — with only a couple of days left, visit a local supermarket (Maxi Pali or BM are budget-friendly chains) and pick up ingredients for a beach picnic dinner. Enjoy a sunset picnic on the beach with local cheeses, bread, fruit, and a bottle of local wine or beer.

meals.breakfast: Pre-rafting energy breakfast — scrambled eggs with rice, beans, and plantains. Budget ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Often included with rafting tour — typically a simple buffet. Budget included or ~$5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Beach picnic with supermarket finds. Budget ~$10–15 USD for a spread for one person

day_by_day.notes: For white-water rafting, listen carefully to the safety briefing and follow all guide instructions. Secure all belongings in waterproof bags. Most operators provide helmets and life jackets. Book the day before to confirm availability and transportation pickup times.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife morning — wake up before sunrise for a golden hour beach walk or forest birding session. Bring your camera for the best lighting. Try to tick off any wildlife from your wish list you haven't spotted yet — ask locals or your resort staff for tips on best spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and packing. Visit local artisan markets for last-minute gifts — look for sustainably made items like wooden carvings, handmade jewelry, and locally grown coffee or chocolate. Avoid mass-produced items — support local artisans directly. Start packing your bags.
day_by_day.evening: CELEBRATION DINNER — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate an amazing 13-day adventure. Look for a local restaurant with ocean views. Try the national dish — Casado — one final time, or splurge on fresh lobster or shrimp if budget allows. Toast to an incredible trip!

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at a beachside café — fresh tropical fruit plate, coffee, and toast. Budget ~$5–8 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch while shopping — street food snacks and fresh coconut water. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — allow a slightly higher budget for this meal. Budget ~$15–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to avoid morning rush. Check airline baggage rules — liquid souvenirs (hot sauce, liqueur) must be in checked luggage. Keep important documents (passport, boarding pass, insurance) in your carry-on. Set an alarm with plenty of buffer time for your departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica! Wake up early for one last beach sunrise — a perfect send-off. Take a final dip in the ocean or simply sit and soak in the sounds of the jungle and waves. Check out of the resort, store luggage with reception if needed, and enjoy a final Tico breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport via pre-booked shared shuttle (book in advance — $15–25 USD). Allow at least 3–4 hours before your flight for travel time and airport procedures. Browse duty-free for last-minute gifts (local coffee and chocolate are great buys). Board your flight home with incredible memories!
day_by_day.evening: In transit home — reflect on your 13-day Costa Rican eco-adventure. Review your photos, start writing trip reviews to help future budget travelers, and begin dreaming of your next adventure. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Gallo Pinto breakfast — a proper Costa Rican send-off at a local soda. Budget ~$4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks packed from the morning — budget airport options or bring your own. Budget ~$8–12 USD
meals.dinner: On the plane or upon arrival home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your shuttle pickup time the evening before. Keep $29 USD cash for the Costa Rica exit tax if not already included in your airfare (most modern tickets include it — check your booking). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Say ¡Pura Vida! to everyone you meet — it's the Costa Rican way of life!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack at the airport or a late-night welcome drink at the resort bar if available upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance. Keep a small amount of Costa Rican colones (CRC) handy for tips. Do not schedule anything early on Day 2 — rest is essential after a late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimate to the tropical climate, observe coastal birds, and get your bearings. Pick up any supplies (sunscreen, insect repellent, water bottles) at a nearby pharmacy or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area surrounding the resort on foot or by taxi. Visit a nearby farmers market or town center to sample fresh tropical fruits like maracuyá, guanábana, and pipas (green coconuts). Stop by a local tour desk to confirm all upcoming excursion bookings.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing sunset on the beach. Head to a nearby mid-range seafood restaurant for a classic Costa Rican casado (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and fresh fish). Return to the resort for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — enjoy gallo pinto (rice and beans), fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort — try a casado or arroz con pollo for an authentic and affordable meal (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront seafood restaurant — grilled red snapper or shrimp ceviche with a local Imperial beer (~$20–30 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery and orientation day. Hydrate well — the tropical humidity can be intense for newcomers. Apply sunscreen even on overcast days.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private shuttle or shared transfer toward Tortuguero National Park (approx. 3–4 hours including a boat transfer through jungle canals). Arrive and check in at a Tortuguero jungle lodge for a one-night stay. Enjoy a welcome lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari — Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, howler monkeys, Jesus Christ lizards, and a spectacular array of tropical birds including toucans and kingfishers. Your certified naturalist guide will use spotting scopes to enhance wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.evening: After the river safari, take a short guided night walk along the jungle trails near the lodge to spot nocturnal wildlife including red-eyed tree frogs, insects, and sleeping birds. Return to the lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the resort before departure — pack fruit, granola bars, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the Tortuguero jungle lodge — typical Costa Rican fare with rice, beans, chicken, and fresh juice (~included or $12–15 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge restaurant — enjoy heart of palm salad, plantain soup, and grilled chicken or fish (~$18–25 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small plane — no roads lead in. Pack light for the overnight stay. Bring waterproof bags for camera equipment. February is dry season in many parts of Costa Rica but Tortuguero receives year-round rainfall — pack a lightweight rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for an optional early-morning canal kayaking session — the best time to spot wildlife as animals are most active at sunrise. Look for manatees, caimans, and hundreds of bird species along the waterways. Return to the lodge for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back from Tortuguero by boat and shuttle toward the Arenal Volcano region (approx. 4–5 hours). Check in to a mid-range eco-lodge near La Fortuna with views of Arenal Volcano. Rest and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the charming town of La Fortuna. Browse local artisan shops and pick up handcrafted souvenirs. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in town with a view of the illuminated volcano.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and coffee before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside soda stop during the transfer — try a tortilla con queso or empanadas (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: La Fortuna town restaurant — try Soda Viquez or a similar local favorite for casado or a hearty beef stew (olla de carne) (~$12–18 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Tortuguero to Arenal is long — bring entertainment, snacks, and a neck pillow. The boat portion is scenic and enjoyable. Book your Arenal eco-lodge in advance as quality mid-range options fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs — Begin with the hanging bridges experience: walk a series of suspension bridges through primary old-growth rainforest surrounding the iconic Arenal Volcano. A naturalist guide will help you spot toucans, morpho butterflies, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys. The elevated bridges offer stunning canopy-level views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges, visit the Arenal 1968 Lava Fields — a self-guided trail through the hardened lava flow from the 1968 eruption with dramatic volcano views. In the late afternoon, head to one of the region's mid-range natural hot springs (such as Baldi or Eco Termales) to soak in the mineral-rich geothermal pools surrounded by tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Continue soaking in the hot springs into the early evening (most complexes include dinner packages). Alternatively, return to La Fortuna for dinner and a peaceful night at the eco-lodge.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast — gallo pinto, fresh fruit, eggs, and local coffee with a volcano view.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at the hanging bridges visitor center or a packed lunch — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Hot springs dinner package (included with some resorts) or La Fortuna restaurant — try Don Rufino's for a mid-range sit-down dinner with grilled meats and local specialties (~$20–28 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking shoes with good grip for the hanging bridges. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot springs. The hot springs are especially magical in the evening — the cooler air contrasts beautifully with the warm thermal waters.

day_by_day.morning: Optional sunrise hike to the Arenal Observatory or Cerro Chato trail base for panoramic volcano views. Return for breakfast, then pack up and prepare for the journey toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approx. 3–4 hours by jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal — a scenic and iconic Costa Rica experience).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde/Santa Elena. Check in to a mid-range cloud forest lodge. Explore the charming Santa Elena town on foot — browse local cheese shops (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), coffee cooperatives, and artisan markets.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local serpentarium or frog pond for a guided night tour to observe dozens of colorful frog species, including the iconic red-eyed tree frog, in their natural habitat. Return for a cozy dinner near the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast in Arenal before departure — eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena upon arrival — try Taco Taco or a local soda for affordable, fresh food (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant in Santa Elena — excellent mid-range Costa Rican cuisine with vegetarian options and a cozy atmosphere (~$15–22 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal is a beloved Costa Rica experience and far more scenic than the road route. Book in advance. Monteverde is cooler and mistier than the lowlands — pack a fleece or light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. The Original Canopy Tour or Sky Adventures offer multiple lines, Tarzan swings, and hanging bridges with breathtaking views above the cloud forest. This is an adrenaline-pumping highlight of the entire trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon walk. The reserve is home to over 400 bird species including the resplendent quetzal (February is an excellent month to spot them), 100+ mammal species, and thousands of plant species. Rent binoculars at the entrance if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an optional guided bat jungle tour or simply enjoy the cool evening air in Santa Elena. Visit a local chocolate tour to learn about cacao farming and sample artisan chocolate. Relax at the lodge with a warm cup of local coffee.

meals.breakfast: Cloud forest lodge breakfast — pancakes, gallo pinto, fresh juice, and Monteverde coffee.
meals.lunch: Café Colibri near the reserve entrance — fresh sandwiches, soups, and smoothies with hummingbird garden views (~$10–15 USD).
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena — unique dining inside and around a giant fig tree, serving burgers, pasta, and Costa Rican dishes (~$16–24 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line tour at least 24 hours in advance — it's extremely popular. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. February offers some of the best chances to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde as they descend to lower elevations during nesting season.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided bird-watching walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve or Children's Eternal Rainforest with a specialist guide. February is peak season for quetzal sightings — a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife experience. Return for a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde by shuttle toward Manuel Antonio on the Pacific Coast (approx. 4–5 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Central Valley and down to the coast. Check in at a mid-range hotel near Manuel Antonio National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and walk to the beach for sunset. Quepos town (5 minutes from Manuel Antonio) has a lively evening scene with excellent restaurants and bars along the marina. Enjoy a casual seaside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure — gallo pinto, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during transfer — try a local soda in Quepos or grab fresh fruit from a roadside vendor (~$6–10 USD).
meals.dinner: El Avión Restaurant in Manuel Antonio — housed inside a retired 1954 Fairchild C-123 cargo plane, serving excellent seafood and tropical cocktails with Pacific Ocean views (~$22–32 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Monteverde to Manuel Antonio passes through some of Costa Rica's most beautiful countryside. Consider a stop at a roadside waterfall or viewpoint along the way. Quepos is the gateway town to Manuel Antonio — most services and restaurants are located here.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike — Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal hidden wildlife. Spot all four monkey species (howler, white-faced capuchin, squirrel, and spider monkeys), two-toed sloths, Jesus Christ lizards, and vibrant tropical birds. The park also features stunning white-sand beaches perfect for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, relax on Playa Biesanz or Playa Manuel Antonio — two of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches inside the park. Snorkel in the calm protected waters, observe raccoons and squirrel monkeys on the beach, and soak up the Pacific sunshine. Exit the park by 4:00 PM (closing time).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Quepos for a casual evening. Browse the Quepos waterfront and marina. Enjoy a sundowner cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Pacific before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — fresh fruit, eggs, and coffee before entering the park early.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach inside Manuel Antonio National Park — sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. (No food vendors inside the park.)
meals.dinner: La Cantina or Sancho's Restaurant in Quepos — lively atmosphere serving tacos, ceviche, and grilled fish with ocean views (~$15–22 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Manuel Antonio National Park as early as possible (opens at 7:00 AM) — wildlife is most active in the morning and the park has a daily visitor cap. Book your guided naturalist tour in advance. Keep all food secured in your bag as the monkeys are notorious thieves! Apply reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Optional sea kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding tour along the Manuel Antonio coastline — explore sea caves, rocky outcroppings, and spot marine wildlife including dolphins, sea turtles, and pelicans from the water. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed morning at the resort beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Manuel Antonio by shuttle toward the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado region (approx. 4–5 hours to Drake Bay or Puerto Jiménez). This remote, wild region is accessible by small charter plane or long land transfer. Check in to a jungle eco-lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the remote jungle lodge atmosphere. Enjoy a guided evening walk around the lodge grounds — the Osa Peninsula has extraordinary nocturnal wildlife including tapirs, peccaries, and ocelots. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Manuel Antonio before departure — gallo pinto, tropical fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during transfer or stop at a roadside soda in Palmar Norte (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Jungle eco-lodge dinner — fresh, locally sourced Costa Rican cuisine often featuring heart of palm, fresh fish, and tropical fruits (~included or $18–25 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is one of Costa Rica's most remote and wild destinations. Roads can be rough — a 4x4 vehicle is recommended. Alternatively, consider a short domestic flight from Quepos/San José to Drake Bay or Puerto Jiménez (~$80–120 USD) to save travel time. Book the lodge well in advance as options are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition — Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' This full-day guided expedition takes you deep into Corcovado's primary rainforest. Your expert guide will track Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, four species of monkeys, scarlet macaws, harpy eagles, and if extremely lucky, a jaguar or puma. The park's untouched wilderness is unlike anywhere else in Costa Rica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition into the afternoon, exploring different trail sections and habitats. Swim in a freshwater jungle river or waterfall. Observe the incredible biodiversity of the rainforest floor, canopy, and everything in between. This is a true bucket-list wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge by boat or trail (depending on entry point). Rest, shower, and share stories of the day's wildlife sightings over dinner. The lodge may offer a naturalist presentation about Osa Peninsula conservation efforts.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before the full-day expedition — high-energy foods: eggs, bread, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the lodge or guide service, eaten in the jungle — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, and plenty of water.
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge dinner — celebrate the incredible day with a hearty meal of fresh catch, rice, beans, and tropical desserts (~included or $20–28 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance permits and a certified guide — arrange this through your lodge or a licensed tour operator well before arrival. Wear long pants, long sleeves, and sturdy waterproof hiking boots. Bring insect repellent, a rain jacket, and a dry bag for electronics. This is a physically demanding full day — pace yourself and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the Osa Peninsula. Options include a guided dolphin and whale-watching boat tour in the Golfo Dulce (the warm gulf waters are home to resident spinner dolphins and humpback whales), a mangrove kayaking tour, or a relaxed beach walk to spot scarlet macaws — which fly in flocks over the Osa coastline in spectacular numbers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the Osa Peninsula by shuttle or domestic flight back toward the Central Valley or your resort area. If returning to the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront, allow 5–6 hours of travel. Use transfer time to reflect on the trip and organize photos and notes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome-back dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby beachfront spot. Toast to an incredible eco-adventure with a local craft beer or a classic guaro sour (Costa Rica's signature spirit).

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast on the Osa — gallo pinto, fresh juice, eggs, and coffee while listening to the jungle wake up.
meals.lunch: Lunch during transfer — roadside soda or packed snacks (~$6–10 USD).
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby beachfront restaurant — splurge slightly on your second-to-last night with grilled lobster, fresh ceviche, and a tropical cocktail (~$25–35 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: If flying domestically from Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay, book your flight well in advance through SANSA or Green Airways. Domestic flights in Costa Rica are small (5–12 seat Cessnas) — baggage weight limits are strict (12–15 kg total). The views from the small planes over the Osa Peninsula and Pacific coastline are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk along the shoreline, do some final wildlife spotting (coastal birds, iguanas, and monkeys are often seen near beachfront resorts), and reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Costa Rica. Swim in the ocean one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Depending on your departure flight, either head directly to Juan Santamaría International Airport (allow 2.5–3.5 hours depending on location) or enjoy a final lunch stop in San José's Mercado Central — a vibrant indoor market where you can pick up last-minute souvenirs: local coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and handcrafted goods at excellent prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with unforgettable memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, jungle rivers, and extraordinary wildlife. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out with the full buffet: fresh tropical fruit, gallo pinto, pastries, eggs, and multiple cups of Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Mercado Central in San José or airport restaurant — casado, empanadas, or a fresh fruit smoothie for a final taste of Costa Rica (~$8–15 USD).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for departure — San José airport can be busy on weekends. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international flights. Declare any agricultural products (coffee, fresh fruit) at customs. Costa Rica has an airport departure tax that is typically included in modern airline tickets — verify with your carrier. Leave a tip for your hotel staff in colones — tipping culture is appreciated throughout Costa Rica. ¡Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged wildlife including white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and Jesus Christ lizards. The hike concludes at a stunning Pacific beach for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest around the iconic Arenal Volcano, observing toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys up close. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by lush jungle, a perfect reward after a day of eco-exploration.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition
experiences.description: Venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' This guided day trek through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest offers unmatched chances to spot all four Costa Rican monkey species, Baird's tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and the endangered scarlet macaw in their pristine natural habitat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome amenity: chilled tropical fruit platter, artisan chocolates, and a complimentary glass of Costa Rican sparkling wine prepared by the resort butler. Light room-service supper available until midnight.

meals.breakfast: On-board or in-airport dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: On-board or in-airport dining prior to arrival
meals.dinner: In-room late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort – curated welcome board with local cheeses, charcuterie, tropical fruits, and a signature Costa Rican herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged and confirmed. Porter service and express check-in should be coordinated with the resort concierge in advance. Luggage handling included. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort orientation morning. Sleep in and enjoy a slow start. Take a guided resort property walk at 9:00 AM led by the resident naturalist to spot toucans, scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and iguanas on the beachfront grounds. Ideal for gentle wildlife observation and acclimatization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beachfront yoga session at 12:30 PM followed by an afternoon at the resort's infinity pool and spa. Book a 90-minute Costa Rican volcanic mud wrap and deep-tissue massage at the resort spa to recover from travel fatigue. Explore the beach and surrounding coastal vegetation at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's ocean-view terrace bar. Enjoy handcrafted Guaro Sours and fresh ceviche bites as the sun dips into the Pacific. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort's ocean-view breakfast buffet featuring tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, Costa Rican gallo pinto, eggs to order, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty Costa Rican single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch – grilled fresh catch of the day with hearts of palm salad, coconut rice, and chilled agua fresca
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – multi-course tasting menu featuring Costa Rican farm-to-table ingredients: sea bass ceviche, palm heart bisque, grilled beef tenderloin with yuca purée, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to allow guests to recover from the late arrival. Spa bookings should be made through the concierge first thing in the morning. Resort naturalist walks are typically complimentary for guests.

day_by_day.morning: Depart at 6:00 AM via private luxury 4x4 vehicle for Tortuguero National Park (approximately 3–4 hours depending on resort location). Arrive and board a private canopied riverboat for the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari. Paddle through the jungle waterways spotting caimans, river otters, green sea turtles, manatees, Jesus Christ lizards, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds with your certified naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark for a guided walking tour of Tortuguero village and its surrounding jungle trails. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the region's critical turtle nesting programs. Enjoy a private picnic lunch on the riverbank prepared by your resort chef.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort via private vehicle. Arrive back approximately 6:00–7:00 PM. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-departure breakfast box prepared by the resort – croissants, tropical fruit, hard-boiled eggs, local cheese, and thermos of Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet riverside picnic prepared by resort chef – chilled shrimp wraps, quinoa salad with mango vinaigrette, fresh coconut water, and artisan cookies
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront restaurant – grilled lobster tail with chimichurri, roasted plantains, coconut cream soup, and a local craft beer or glass of Chilean Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible by boat or small plane; confirm the most efficient route from the resort's specific location with the concierge. February is an excellent month for bird watching and wildlife spotting. Bring insect repellent, binoculars, and a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private birdwatching excursion at 5:30 AM along the resort's coastal and forest edge with the resident ornithologist. Spot scarlet macaws, toucans, motmots, and migratory species. Return for a full resort breakfast by 8:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs at 10:30 AM toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours). Check into a luxury eco-lodge near Arenal for the next two nights. Afternoon at leisure exploring the lodge's private rainforest trails and lakeside views of the volcano.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Arenal Volcano from the lodge terrace. Soak in the lodge's private natural hot spring pool as the sky turns crimson. Dinner at the lodge's acclaimed restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast at Aegean Bliss – eggs Benedict with smoked local fish, fresh tropical fruit platter, artisan pastries, and Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: En-route stop at a premium roadside restaurant or packed gourmet lunch box – chicken empanadas, fresh fruit, local cheese, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Arenal eco-lodge restaurant – wood-fired Costa Rican beef short rib with cassava cake, hearts of palm salad, and a local Segua craft lager or glass of Malbec

day_by_day.notes: Arenal Volcano is one of Costa Rica's most iconic landmarks. The lodge should be pre-selected for its proximity to hot springs and primary rainforest. February is generally dry season on the Pacific side but can be mixed near Arenal – pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs experience begins at 7:30 AM. Walk a series of spectacular suspension bridges through primary old-growth rainforest with a certified naturalist guide. Observe sloths, howler monkeys, poison dart frogs, toucans, and extraordinary flora at canopy level. Stunning close-up views of Arenal Volcano throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges, transfer to a premium private hot springs resort (such as Tabacón or Baldi) for a 3-hour soak in the naturally heated volcanic mineral pools surrounded by lush jungle. Enjoy poolside service with fresh tropical cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge. Enjoy a private couples' or solo candlelit dinner on a terrace with volcano views, arranged by the lodge concierge. Stargazing session with the lodge's telescope if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – Costa Rican-style gallo pinto, fresh eggs, plantains, local white cheese, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Hot springs resort poolside restaurant – grilled fish tacos, ceviche, tropical fruit bowl, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private candlelit terrace dinner at the eco-lodge – filet mignon with volcanic salt crust, roasted root vegetables, truffle yuca purée, and a premium Costa Rican chocolate lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges circuit is approximately 3 km and takes 2–3 hours at a naturalist's pace. Comfortable hiking shoes and light moisture-wicking clothing recommended. Binoculars are essential. Hot springs visit should be pre-booked for a private or semi-private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal at 7:00 AM and travel to Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 2.5–3 hours via private 4x4). Check into a premium cloud forest lodge. After settling in, begin the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour at 11:00 AM. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuit, with platforms reaching 200 feet above the forest floor and lines stretching over a kilometer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-zip-line, enjoy a guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve with a certified naturalist. Spot resplendent quetzals (February is prime quetzal season!), three-wattled bellbirds, emerald toucanets, and rare orchids in the ethereal mist.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge. Enjoy a craft cocktail at the lodge's misty mountain bar before dinner. Evening night walk in the cloud forest with a guide to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tree frogs, and sleeping birds.

meals.breakfast: En-route breakfast at a premium café in the Arenal-Monteverde corridor or packed lodge breakfast box – granola, yogurt, tropical fruits, and thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Monteverde town premium restaurant – wood-fired pizza with hearts of palm and local cheese, fresh salad, and artisan lemonade
meals.dinner: Cloud forest lodge restaurant – cream of mushroom and cloud forest herb bisque, slow-braised local chicken in achiote sauce with rice and beans, and tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde as it is their pre-nesting season. Request a quetzal-specialist guide through the lodge. The zip-line tour should be booked in advance; the Original Canopy Tour or Extremo Park are top premium options.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated quetzal and rare wildlife morning walk at 6:00 AM in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve with a private expert ornithologist guide. The reserve's primary cloud forest is home to over 400 bird species. Walk misty trails draped in bromeliads and orchids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Orchid Garden for an immersive close-up look at the region's extraordinary biodiversity. Afternoon coffee and chocolate tasting experience at a premium local artisan producer – learn the farm-to-cup and farm-to-bar story of Costa Rican cacao and coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over the Gulf of Nicoya from the Monteverde ridge (on clear days, spectacular). Farewell dinner at the cloud forest lodge before preparing for the next leg of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Early light pre-walk snack at 5:45 AM – energy bars, banana, and thermos of coffee. Full hot breakfast upon return at the lodge: eggs, gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruits, and pastries
meals.lunch: Artisan café in Monteverde – avocado toast on homemade sourdough, local cheese board, fresh-pressed green juice, and artisan chocolate samples
meals.dinner: Cloud forest lodge signature dinner – four-course meal: cream of chayote soup, mixed greens with mango dressing, braised beef tenderloin in Guaro reduction with yuca fries, and passion fruit cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve requires advance reservations and limits daily visitor numbers. Book through the lodge concierge well in advance. The morning walk should begin before sunrise for the best quetzal sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde to Manuel Antonio (approximately 4–5 hours via private 4x4 with scenic stops). Stop at a viewpoint overlooking the Central Valley and at a premium roadside artisan market for unique Costa Rican crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Manuel Antonio region. Check into a luxury boutique hotel or jungle villa with ocean views. Afternoon at leisure – explore the hotel's private pool and jungle gardens. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys and sloths from the hotel terrace, which is common in this area.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Dinner at one of Manuel Antonio's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Cloud forest lodge farewell breakfast – full Costa Rican spread with gallo pinto, eggs, plantains, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: En-route gourmet stop at a premium restaurant in Quepos – fresh tuna sashimi, ceviche mixto, coconut rice, and tropical agua fresca
meals.dinner: El Patio de Café Milagro or equivalent premium Manuel Antonio restaurant – sesame-crusted ahi tuna, grilled jumbo shrimp with tamarind glaze, and a local craft cocktail

day_by_day.notes: The Quepos/Manuel Antonio area is approximately 3.5 hours from San José and best reached by private vehicle for comfort and flexibility. Book the luxury boutique hotel in advance as February is high season. White-faced capuchin monkeys are very active at dusk around hotel gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Hike begins at 7:00 AM (park opens early and wildlife is most active at dawn). Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins, squirrel monkeys (endemic and endangered), scarlet macaws, Jesus Christ lizards, and boa constrictors.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, relax on the pristine white sand beaches inside the national park – Playa Manuel Antonio is consistently ranked among the world's most beautiful beaches. Enjoy snorkeling in the crystal-clear waters of the marine park around the rocky headlands, spotting colorful reef fish and sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel. Sunset yoga on the hotel terrace. Private chef dinner experience at the villa or hotel suite.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at hotel – light and energizing: yogurt parfait with granola and tropical fruits, hard-boiled eggs, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic inside the park or at a premium beach restaurant just outside the park entrance – grilled fish sandwich, fresh ceviche, coconut water, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience – five-course tasting menu featuring the day's freshest catch: lobster bisque, mango caprese, grilled snapper with herb oil, beef medallion with chimichurri, and a Costa Rican chocolate and coffee mousse

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers strictly – reservations must be made well in advance, especially in February (high season). Guides must be hired outside the park entrance. Bring biodegradable sunscreen (required in the park), water, and binoculars. Squirrel monkeys are critically endangered – observe from a respectful distance.

day_by_day.morning: Private sportfishing or whale-watching boat charter departs at 6:30 AM from Quepos Marina. February is excellent for whale watching (humpback whales migrate through these waters) and world-class offshore fishing for marlin, sailfish, and dorado. Choose your preferred experience with the captain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to marina by 1:00 PM. Afternoon visit to a premium wellness spa in Manuel Antonio for a 2-hour treatment: volcanic stone massage, botanical body scrub, and hydrotherapy. Complete relaxation before the next expedition.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a clifftop restaurant with panoramic Pacific Ocean views. Toast to the halfway point of the journey.

meals.breakfast: Early morning on-boat breakfast prepared by the charter crew – fresh fruit, pastries, yogurt, and thermos of coffee while watching the sunrise over the Pacific
meals.lunch: Quepos waterfront premium restaurant – catch-of-the-day ceviche, grilled mahi-mahi tacos, fresh coconut water, and artisan ice cream
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant (or equivalent clifftop fine dining) – Mediterranean-Costa Rican fusion: grilled octopus, fresh pasta with local seafood, and a premium glass of Spanish Albariño

day_by_day.notes: February is peak humpback whale season in the Southern Pacific of Costa Rica. Confirm with the charter company the best option (fishing vs. whale watching) based on current conditions. A 4–6 hour private charter is recommended for the full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure at 5:30 AM via private 4x4 transfer to the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado National Park (approximately 3–4 hours to the park entrance). Begin the Corcovado National Park Jungle Expedition – venture into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' Your expert guide leads you through primary old-growth rainforest teeming with tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, four species of monkeys, harpy eagles, and the iconic scarlet macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition deep into the park's interior trails. Visit a jungle waterfall for a refreshing swim in a pristine natural pool. Spot poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and ancient ceiba trees draped in bromeliads. This is a once-in-a-lifetime immersive wilderness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to a luxury eco-lodge on the Osa Peninsula (Drake Bay or Puerto Jiménez area) for an overnight stay. Dinner at the lodge under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Pre-departure packed breakfast box – energy bars, banana, hard-boiled eggs, cheese, and thermos of coffee consumed en route
meals.lunch: Jungle expedition gourmet packed lunch prepared by the lodge – chicken wraps, tropical fruit, trail mix, chocolate, and purified water
meals.dinner: Osa Peninsula eco-lodge dinner – fresh-caught local fish in coconut curry, plantain rice, hearts of palm salad, and a glass of premium Chilean red wine under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is one of the most remote and pristine national parks in the world. Access requires advance permits and certified guides. February is dry season on the Osa Peninsula – ideal conditions. Wear long sleeves, sturdy hiking boots, and bring a dry bag for camera equipment. Leeches and insects are common – insect repellent is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn wildlife walk at 5:30 AM on the Osa Peninsula's private eco-lodge trails. Spot scarlet macaws flying in pairs at sunrise (the Osa has the largest scarlet macaw population in Central America), as well as tapirs near the river. Private kayaking or paddleboarding through the Golfo Dulce mangroves with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury charter flight from Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay back to San José or directly to the resort region (approximately 45 minutes). This scenic flight over the rainforest and Pacific coastline is spectacular. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon at leisure – pool, beach, or spa.
day_by_day.evening: Special premium farewell dinner experience at the resort – private beach dinner setup with torchlight, a personal butler, and a curated five-course menu paired with premium wines.

meals.breakfast: Osa eco-lodge breakfast – fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto, eggs to order, local white cheese, and specialty Osa Peninsula coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box or light lunch upon arrival back at the resort – ceviche, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private torchlit beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – five-course paired menu: champagne with oysters, lobster bisque, seared tuna tataki, grilled wagyu beef with chimichurri and truffle yuca, and a decadent Costa Rican cacao and rum chocolate fondant with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The private charter flight from the Osa Peninsula is the most efficient and scenic way to return. Book through Sansa Air or Nature Air well in advance. The private beach dinner should be arranged with the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance and will require specific weather conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sunrise walk along the beachfront. Last opportunity to spot wildlife in the resort gardens. Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast. Last swim in the ocean or infinity pool. Visit the resort gift shop for premium Costa Rican coffee, artisan chocolate, and local crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out and private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport for departure. Allow 3 hours before flight for international check-in, customs, and departure lounge time. Enjoy the airport's premium lounge if available.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and luxury.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort – full à la carte menu: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, tropical fruit platter, freshly baked pastries, smoothie bowl, and a final cup of Costa Rican single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport premium lounge – club sandwich, fresh salad, and a glass of sparkling wine
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with the concierge based on your specific flight schedule. Request an express check-out to maximize your final morning at the resort. Ensure all purchased wildlife products comply with CITES regulations – Costa Rican customs is strict about biological materials. A heartfelt tip for the resort staff and guides who made the journey exceptional is customary and appreciated.
